subject: Clarify license scope for private deployment replication & audit inventory
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: contracting@heliohealth.com
Date: 2026-04-17T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Question on license boundary for private deployment DR/replication

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form — team has a couple of follow-ups specific to our private deployment plans. We will be deploying your software inside our VPC and want to replicate inference workloads across two sites (primary + warm DR). Our security group is asking for a clear statement on: 1) whether replication between sites counts as a separate licensed environment; 2) what artifacts (snapshots, images) we are entitled to keep for audit and forensic purposes; and 3) any limits on number of operator accounts for on-prem installations.

I attached the redline our procurement team started. Can your legal/ops team confirm whether the license scope in Section 2 covers cross-site replication or whether we need an exhibit for multi-site instantiation? Also, please outline the evidence we can present to auditors showing custody of snapshots without transferring IP.

We need answers by end of week to keep our compliance review on track.

— Maria
Head of Procurement, HelioHealth

Attachments: redline_MSA_v3.docx
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>, contracting@heliohealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-17T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on license boundary for private deployment DR/replication

Maria — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Looping in Laura (legal) and David (solutions) to confirm annotations and produce a short evidence inventory. Quick answers up-front: 1) Our standard MSA license scope treats a single deployed tenant (customer-controlled infra) as one licensed deployment; replication for DR that does not create independently routable production endpoints is usually covered. 2) Snapshots and forensic artifacts are allowed for auditing, but there are constraints around export of model binaries — we typically permit encrypted snapshots plus a signed attestation rather than handing over raw weights. 3) Operator account counts are negotiable; the order form has a default of 5 operator users; we can propose an expanded operator bundle if you need more.

Laura / David — can you confirm the above and propose specific language for an exhibit that clarifies: multi-site warm DR being included vs. full active-active (which we treat as separate licensing), allowed artifact types, and an attestation template Helio can present to auditors? I will also draft a short runbook fragment for the snapshot custody flow.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-18T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on license boundary for private deployment DR/replication

Hi all,

Reviewed Maria's redlines and Rishi's summary. Proposed positions below — these will be placed into an MSA exhibit and mirrored in the order form exhibit:  

- License boundary: "Licensed Deployment" means a single customer-controlled environment. Warm DR (passive replica used only for failover and not for serving concurrent production traffic) is included. Active-active serving across multiple sites will be treated as additional licensed deployments and billed accordingly.
- Snapshot & artifact retention: Customer may retain encrypted snapshots, encrypted configuration bundles, and operation logs for audit and forensic purposes. Redwood will not be required to provide raw model binaries or proprietary build artifacts. For export, an attestation flow will be used: Redwood signs a custody attestation confirming the snapshot contents and chain-of-custody; customer retains encrypted snapshot.
- Operator accounts: Default operator seat count = 5. Additional seats available as priced in the order form. For audits, we can provide temporary read-only observer accounts for auditors with time-limited tokens; operator credentials for Redwood staff require court-approved or contractually defined witness protocols.

Requested action: Rishi / David, please review the technical runbook wording below and confirm if the snapshot attestation flow is implementable as-is. If yes, I'll incorporate language into an exhibit and send a clean redline.

Proposed runbook fragment (for legal review):
1) Snapshot generation: Customer initiates on-prem snapshot via provided tooling; snapshot is encrypted with customer KMS.
2) Integrity verification: Redwood artifacts tool runs a content hash and produces a signed digest.
3) Attestation: Redwood signs an attestation statement (PDF) listing included components and a hash; the attestation references time and operator identity.
4) Audit access: Customer may present the encrypted snapshot plus attestation to auditors; Redwood will, upon mutually agreed process, allow controlled witnessing of restoration in a sandbox environment without transferring raw weights.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_exhibit_text.docx (will send once David confirms)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-19T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on license boundary for private deployment DR/replication

Thanks — technical confirmation below. We think the proposed exhibit and runbook fragment are implementable with these clarifications: 

- Warm DR definition: must be passive (no steady-state serving) and placed behind a failover switch. Telemetry must show single active serving endpoint. We can add a heartbeat/time-based cutover guard in the runbook to avoid license ambiguity.
- Snapshot contents: our tooling will exclude model training artifacts and any proprietary kernel caches. Snapshots will include model weights in an encrypted container, runtime config, and inference logs as agreed.
- Attestation format: we can produce a signed SHA-256 digest and a human-readable attestation PDF. Signing will use Redwood's code-signing key; if Helio requires a third-party notary, we can accommodate a timestamped witness run under an NDA.
- Operator accounts and audit observer access: we can deliver a single auditor read-only token for a defined window; creation of additional operator seats will be added to the order form as an optional line item.

I've attached the initial runbook draft (privdeploy_runbook_draft.pdf) with entries that map to the legal language. If Laura approves, we can populate the exhibit and I will create a short demo script for the auditor walk-through.

— David
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachments: privdeploy_runbook_draft.pdf
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@heliohealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on license boundary for private deployment DR/replication

Laura / David — this is helpful, thank you. Two quick asks before we finalize the exhibit: 1) Can you add a short, one-paragraph example that describes an acceptable failover test and how it would be evidenced to an auditor? 2) For the attestation, would Redwood be willing to include an indexed manifest (list of filenames + hashes) as part of the signed attestation? Helio's auditors prefer an itemized manifest.

If you can incorporate those two items in the exhibit text, procurement can sign off and we can move to order form pricing for the extra operator seats. Suggest a 30-minute call Wednesday to walk the auditor through the runbook demo.

Regards,
Maria
Head of Procurement, HelioHealth
